outcome: No result found since 26 January 2024 that changes the Kaplan-Yorke conjecture as stated (that the Lyapunov dimension of a 'typical' dynamical system's attractor equals its information/Hausdorff dimension); all located post-window work addresses namesake variants (delay differential equations) rather than the stated conjecture.
summary: The Kaplan-Yorke conjecture (Kaplan and Yorke, 1979) holds that for a 'typical' dissipative dynamical system, the Lyapunov (Kaplan-Yorke) dimension of an attractor equals its information dimension (and, in many treatments, coincides with the Hausdorff/box-counting dimension). The original two-dimensional-map case was proven by Kaplan-Yorke themselves and extended by L.-S. Young (1984) to a class of 2D systems where Lyapunov, Hausdorff, box-counting and Rényi dimensions all coincide; that work predates the window and settled only the low-dimensional case, leaving the general higher-dimensional conjecture open (with known artificial counterexamples such as constructions related to the Feigenbaum attractor showing it fails without genericity assumptions). Extensive searching (WebSearch queries listed below, plus the triage's own three queries) turned up nothing in the 26 January 2024 to present window that advances the general conjecture. The only post-window hits are: (1) Zhang & Wu-type work extending the unrelated 'Kaplan-Yorke formula' (a different, non-namesake concept from delay differential equation theory concerning periodic solutions, not attractor dimension) to infinite-dimensional Banach-space delay systems (Journal of Dynamics and Differential Equations, 2025, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10884-025-10428-4) -- this changes the question (a different dynamical setting and a different formula bearing the same name) rather than restricting it, so it is a related problem, not a case; and (2) a January 2025 ScienceDirect paper on 'Kaplan-Yorke periodic solutions' for delay differential equations, which is an entirely unrelated namesake topic (periodic-orbit multiplicity, not attractor dimension) (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0022039625000440). Neither touches the Lyapunov-dimension-equals-information-dimension conjecture for finite-dimensional attractors as Wikipedia states it. A December 2024 arXiv paper on Rulkov neuron lattices (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.12134) empirically checks that Lyapunov dimension is close to box-counting dimension for one specific system -- this is a numerical illustration consistent with the conjecture for a single example, not a proof, case settlement, or bound movement on the conjecture itself, and does not rise to the level of 'progress'. The Wikipedia article on the conjecture itself (fetched live) has no updates reflecting any 2024-2026 development and cites nothing past 2020. No AI system appears anywhere in this material. I therefore find no change to the conjecture's status and no AI involvement.
competing_reading: One could argue the December 2024 Rulkov-neuron paper constitutes 'progress' in the loose sense of adding a data point consistent with the conjecture holding for a specific chaotic system, similar to how record-verification is sometimes counted for existence questions. But per §3.1, a single-system numerical check is not a bound moving or a case being settled in a way that changes what a careful person would write in the bullet -- it is closer to routine numerical corroboration than to mathematical progress, so I classify it as not counting and keep status as open/no_change_found rather than progress.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or published paper explicitly proving the Kaplan-Yorke/Lyapunov-dimension conjecture (or a genuine restriction of it, e.g. for a specific higher-dimensional class of attractors with an SRB or physical measure) for finite-dimensional dissipative systems, dated after 26 January 2024, or an explicit new counterexample to the conjecture as stated for a 'typical'/generic system.
